audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer labels Nimbus Strike "His escape" in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t, and builds the whole tracking instruction around that.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike is a dash TO a targeted enemy at 650 range — it closes distance, it does not create it. Wukong's escape is Warrior Trickster (W): invisibility plus a dash plus a decoy clone. The content layer gets this right ("E-dash into Q is the early threat") while the full layer gets it backwards, so the two halves of the same page tell the reader opposite things about the same ability.
audit.corrected: Nimbus Strike is his engage — a targeted dash on 10s at rank 1. Warrior Trickster is the escape, on 22s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — E and W descriptions and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: "his crit-heavy autos out-trade you" and "crit autos" attribute critical strike to Wukong's early damage.
audit.why: There is no crit anywhere in the kit. Stone Skin is stacking armor and max-health regeneration; Crushing Blow is bonus damage plus an armor shred plus an auto reset. What actually wins him the early trade is Crushing Blow stripping Nasus's armor before the follow-up autos land. This matters for itemization: a reader told the threat is crit reaches for the wrong defensive answer instead of simply respecting the shred window.
audit.corrected: He has no crit. Crushing Blow's armor shred plus the auto reset is what wins the early trade.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json — P and Q descriptions; no crit mechanic in the kit

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Crushing Blow grants bonus attack range, or gives its per-rank numbers.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Wukong's next attack gains attack range." The range scales 250/275/300/325/350. That is the reason a Wukong can start a trade from a step further out than a melee matchup normally allows, and it grows every point he puts in Q. Against Nasus, whose entire trade pattern is walking into auto range for a stacked Siphoning Strike, being out-spaced at the moment of commitment is the whole difficulty of the lane and it is never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow gains attack range, 250 at rank 1 rising to 350 at rank 5 — he out-spaces your melee auto and shreds armor with the same button.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown number appears anywhere, and breakdown.cooldowns ends with the instruction "Dodge or sidestep it" attached to Warrior Trickster.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is a self-cast invisibility-and-dash; there is nothing to sidestep. The numbers that actually matter are Warrior Trickster at 22/21/20/19/18 — the longest short cooldown in his kit and therefore the real punish window — and Cyclone at 130/110/90, where a single dodged ultimate buys over two minutes at rank 1. Crushing Blow at 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 is the short cooldown that decides individual trades.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster 22s at rank 1 — commit after it, never into it. Cyclone 130s at rank 1. Crushing Blow 8s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content describes Crushing Blow as an armor shred and Warrior Trickster as a decoy clone to bait Wither and Spirit Fire.
audit.why: Both check out against Riot's text — Q "reduces the target's armor", W "leaves behind a clone that will attack nearby enemies". The advice not to spend Wither on the clone is the correct read and worth keeping; I only tightened the naming.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet suspectNames flags "Spirit Fire's" in late as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Spirit Fire is the correct Riot name for Nasus's E, and the edit distance comes from the possessive.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on the level chart, and here it is the content layer that looks wrong.
audit.why: Nasus wins only 49.64% over 828 games. The full layer's phases give Wukong stages 1-4, Skill at 6, Nasus at first and second item — a shape that matches a sub-50% result. The content layer's win[] gives Nasus two stages against Wukong's one with four Skill stages, which reads as a lane Nasus edges. Not submitted as an edit: the ±10% length band cannot turn "Skill" into "Wukong".
audit.corrected: content win[3] and win[4] are the doubtful ones; the full-layer shape is the better match for 49.64%.
sources: packet winRate 49.64 / 828 games; champ-data/content/nasus.js win[], champ-data/nasus.full.js phases[].side

edits.before: His E-dash into Q armor-shred plus crit autos out-trades you here, and you have no Wither yet to peel the engage.
edits.after: Nimbus Strike into Crushing Blow strips your armor and out-trades you here, and you have no Wither yet to peel it.

edits.before: Wukong's E-dash into Q is the early threat — the Q shreds your armor and his crit-heavy autos out-trade you while you have no Wither to slow the engage. Don't contest the wave with autos at level 1-2; soak Q stacks with the tip of Spirit Fire and let your Soul Eater lifesteal heal the poke back. At 3 you finally get Wither, so if he E-dashes in you can ramp the slow on him and walk away from the trade he wanted.
edits.after: Wukong's Nimbus Strike into Crushing Blow is the early threat — Crushing Blow shreds your armor and resets his auto while you have no Wither to slow the engage. He has no crit; the shred is doing the work. Don't contest the wave with autos at level 1-2; soak Q stacks with the tip of Spirit Fire and let your Soul Eater lifesteal heal the poke back. At 3 you finally get Wither, so when he dashes in you ramp the slow and walk away.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay roughly even — he's still item-dependent and can E-Q-auto you, but Wither now turns every one of his engages sour by gutting his attack speed and escape. At 6 respect his R: the spin-knockup will interrupt a Q windup and chain his full combo, so Wither him the instant he dashes and let your Fury of the Sands bonus HP and lifesteal eat the damage. Bait the W clone — don't blow Spirit Fire or Wither on the decoy.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay roughly even — he can still Nimbus Strike into Crushing Blow, but Wither turns every engage sour by gutting his attack speed and his exit. At 6 respect Cyclone: the knockup interrupts your Q and chains his combo, and it is 130s at rank 1, so one survived ult buys you two clean minutes. Wither him the instant he dashes and let Fury of the Sands eat the damage. Never spend Wither or Spirit Fire on the clone.

edits.before: This is where you take over. With Sheen and a stack lead your empowered Q plus Spirit Fire's armor shred out-damages his whole combo, and your lifesteal grinds through his armor stacking faster than he can burst you. His clone is now an escape tool, not a kill tool — Wither him so he can't disengage either. Just hold ult for his R window and the 1v1 is yours; only a fed Wukong roaming off you with picks matters.
edits.after: This is where you take over. With Sheen and a stack lead your empowered Q plus Spirit Fire's armor shred out-damages his whole combo, and it strips the Stone Skin armor he ramps up mid-fight faster than he can burst you. Warrior Trickster is now an escape, not a kill — 22s at rank 1, so punish the window right after it. Hold ult for Cyclone and the 1v1 is yours; only a fed Wukong roaming for picks matters.

notes: The engage/escape inversion on Nimbus Strike is the significant one — it appears three times in the full layer and directly contradicts the content layer on the same page. The best previously-unstated fact recovered here is that Crushing Blow grants bonus attack range scaling 250 to 350 across its ranks, which is why Wukong controls the spacing at the exact moment Nasus needs to step in for a stacked Q. I did not compare that number against Nasus's own Q range: Data Dragon reports 255 for Siphoning Strike, but ddragon's range field for melee auto-reset abilities is not consistently the same measurement across champions, so a direct numeric comparison would not be safe. Unlike the other entries in my slice, here the full-layer level chart looks more accurate than the content-layer one given the 49.64% win rate.
